title: Ctrl-\ does not quit / hangs emulator when program polls CONST
description: When an interactive program busy-polls the console status (CONST) instead of blocking on CONIN, pressing the Ctrl-\ quit key closes the input channel but never sets the eof flag (which is only set in CONIN), so the main loop keeps running and CONST returns false forever -> emulator unresponsive, never exits. Fix: a quit signal the reader thread sets that the main loop checks every iteration, independent of CONIN.
close_reason: Ctrl-\ now raises a quit flag (AtomicBool, set by reader thread) that the run loop checks every step via Console::wants_quit() — works even when a program busy-polls CONST and never calls CONIN. Regression test added; make check green.

title: PACMAN95 hangs at startup ('Wait a few seconds, and type a CR')
description: User reports PACMAN95 freezes interactively after 'Wait a few seconds, and type a CR:'. NOT the same cause as the Turbo Microbee-highlight bug (PACMAN95's early output uses only ESC= (cursor, handled) and one ESC; — no ESC(). Could NOT reproduce headlessly: given CR + menu input (e.g. 'PACMAN95\r\r\rY\rY\r\r') it proceeds, draws the maze, and plays; with no further input it stops at EOF as expected. The 'Wait a few seconds' wording suggests a real-time timing/calibration phase — the interactive freeze may be timing-related (test --mhz=2 vs --fast) or a render/input issue specific to the live TTY. NEED FROM USER: after pressing CR, is the screen blank / garbled / a menu? do keys (1,2,L,I,E) respond? does --mhz=2 or --fast change it? Investigate the post-CR code path and any delay-loop calibration.
notes: RESOLVED. Not a hang and not the ESC( highlight bug. PACMAN95 (Microbee VDU) begins each redraw with ESC ; (clear screen) + ESC = (home). The translator passed ESC ; through; a modern terminal ignores it, so the screen was never cleared — it homed to the top and overdrew the old contents (so it looked frozen/garbled). Fix: translate ESC ; -> ESC[2J ESC[H (added to the clear-screen group with the ADM-3A * / : variants). Verified end-to-end: clear now precedes the dungeon text; unit test added.
close_reason: Closed

title: SUBMIT/$$$.SUB batch files don't chain in the HLE BIOS
description: While verifying BDS C I tried driving 'CC -> CLINK -> run' via 'SUBMIT B' (B.SUB). SUBMIT ran but no commands chained: output was just 'A>SUBMIT B / A>'. The genuine CCP reads A:$$$.SUB after each command/warm-boot; our HLE WBOOT path apparently doesn't hand control back to the CCP in a way that re-reads $$$.SUB, so batch submission is a no-op. PROGRAMS.TXT documents 'SUBMIT FILE' as working, so either fix the warm-boot/$$$.SUB handling or soften that guide line. Repro: add SUBMIT.COM + a .SUB file to an 8MB disk, run 'SUBMIT name'. Note: a prompt-gated test Console (release next command only after seeing 'A>') is the clean way to drive multi-step CP/M sessions headless without type-ahead races.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (corrected): the HLE BIOS / warm-boot / $$$.SUB path is NOT broken.
Traced via instrumentation: SUBMIT.COM does write $$$.SUB and warm-boot, the CCP
detects it (BDOS fn 13) and engages the submit scan. The failure was that the
.SUB file lacked a ^Z (0x1A) end-of-text marker, so SUBMIT read past the content
into the disk's zero-padding, parsed zero commands, and wrote an EMPTY $$$.SUB
(rc=00, no allocation). readcom then computes last-record = rc-1 = 0xFF, the read
fails, and the nosub path deletes $$$.SUB -> nothing chains.

Proof: a ^Z-terminated .SUB chains correctly (SUBMIT B with "STAT\r\n\x1a" runs
STAT and prints "A: R/W, Space: 8116k"). A .SUB authored in-world with ED is
already ^Z-terminated and works; only host-imported .SUB files were affected.

FIX: main.rs terminate_if_submit() appends ^Z to .SUB files at the host-import
boundary (covers `cargo run -- x.sub` and load-all.sh). Binaries left byte-exact.
Unit test added. Also added CpmBios::disk() accessor (used for this diagnosis;
the .dsk image epic 9br.2 will reuse it). PROGRAMS.TXT's SUBMIT line is correct
as-is. Follow-up worth considering: host-imported .TXT files have the same
missing-^Z issue for TYPE (today only PROGRAMS.TXT is ^Z'd, by fetch-software.sh).
close_reason: Closed

title: Monitor core: breakpoints, step, continue
description: Interactive control of execution.
notes: DONE. New module crates/cpemu/src/monitor.rs: Monitor<T: BiosTrap> wraps an Executor and adds breakpoints (BTreeSet, sorted), step() (one instruction/BIOS trap, returns terminal StopReason or None), and run(max_steps) -> StopReason {Breakpoint|Halted|Stopped|Illegal|StepLimit}.
